assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window: the detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos in a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector, followed by evidence for point sources (a flaring blazar, the Galactic plane, a Seyfert galaxy). It is an instrumental and conceptual achievement with clear lasting impact on neutrino astronomy and the origin of cosmic rays. As an experimentalist in astroparticle detectors I judge the engineering and the physics to be tightly coupled and unusually clear.
assessment.attribution: IceCube is a large collaboration, but the idea of a kilometre-scale ice Cherenkov array, its realisation and its leadership are widely associated with Halzen (concept and spokesperson role), with Spiering and Karle prominent in the AMANDA-to-IceCube development. The supplied names support a fair three-person configuration; I cannot independently verify the detailed credit split, and other early pioneers (for example in the DUMAND and Baikal lines) are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux confirmed by independent analysis channels over a decade; individual source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) are still few and statistically moderate, but the discovery of the flux itself is robust. Timing is reasonable, perhaps slightly early for source-level astrophysics.
uncertainties: Source-level associations remain of modest significance and may evolve with more data.
Credit across a very large collaboration and earlier pioneering projects is hard to reduce to three people.
KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD results may refine the picture; I have not verified their status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new organising principle for electronic matter, with a theoretical prediction followed by experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells and 3D materials. The idea has influenced condensed matter, materials and quantum-device research broadly, and is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: The Kane-Mele theoretical papers and the first transport observation by Molenkamp's group form a clean theory-plus-experiment pairing. Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators is also decisive, as are theorists not in the credited list (for example Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore), so a three-person prize inevitably omits some. I propose Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the most defensible core from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups and materials platforms over nearly two decades; interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation between 2D (quantum spin Hall) and 3D (Hasan) topological insulator discoveries is unresolved.
Credited list omits several key theorists, so any configuration is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realising the Hubbard model with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics and single-site microscopy, established quantum simulation as an experimental discipline. Originality and lasting impact are high, with precise control and clean connection to condensed matter theory.
assessment.attribution: The credited set is five people. Zoller (with Jaksch and collaborators) provided the proposal; Bloch and Greiner carried out the Mott transition experiments and quantum-gas microscopy; Esslinger realised fermionic Hubbard physics. Greiner and Cirac are defensible alternatives, so the choice is a judgement among close contributions and the allocation is genuinely unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups replicate and extend the work; the field is mature, although the stated goal of solving open Hubbard-model questions such as d-wave pairing is not yet fully achieved.
uncertainties: Prize configuration limited to three out of five credible names.
Jaksch, who co-authored the key proposal, is not in the credited list.
Overlap with other quantum-simulation recognition may affect timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states opened the field of moire quantum materials. It is original, conceptually clean, and has produced a wide set of follow-on discoveries.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald theoretical prediction together with Jarillo-Herrero's experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity is a natural three-person configuration. Cao, who was first author of the experiments, is not credited and may be considered by others, and other groups contributed to early confirmation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple groups since 2018 and extended to other moire systems, but the pairing mechanism and some phases remain debated, so the field is still evolving. Slightly early but not premature as a recognition of the discovery.
uncertainties: Microscopic nature of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Role of early-career experimentalists not in the credited list.
Sample-to-sample variability has complicated early reproducibility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, achieved fractional uncertainty at the 10^-18 level and enabled tests of relativity, searches for varying constants and prospects for a redefinition of the second. It is an instrument-driven advance with strong lasting impact in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye led the realisation of record accuracy and stability; this two-person credit is clean. Contributions from other groups (for example ion and Sr clock programmes) are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced and compared across laboratories at the 10^-18 level; recognition is timely, though a possible redefinition of the second is still in progress.
uncertainties: Frequency-comb contributions were recognised in 2005, which may affect committee judgement of novelty.
Whether optical clocks are viewed as one discovery or a family of related advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model and is a landmark of experimental particle physics, based on extraordinary detector and analysis efforts. Its scientific importance is beyond doubt, and I regard detector instrumentation as central to the achievement.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical prediction, but the experimental discovery has not been recognised, and the statutes do not allow a collaboration. Attribution across ATLAS and CMS spokespeople and detector pioneers is intrinsically contested, and the credited list has four names for a three-person limit. My selection of Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee is one possible configuration, not a resolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments and extensive follow-up measurements of couplings; the interpretation is stable. Recognition could be considered timely, but the committee has already honoured the underlying discovery.
uncertainties: Fair individual credit in a several-thousand-person collaboration is unresolved.
Committee may feel the Higgs has already been recognised in 2013.
Michel Della Negra is excluded under the three-name limit, which is difficult to justify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductivity (LaFeAsO) created a second family of high-Tc materials, stimulating large experimental and theoretical efforts. The discovery is clear and has had a long-lasting impact on unconventional superconductivity.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono are the discovering authors in the 2008 report and the credit is simple. Subsequent rapid contributions by Chinese groups raising Tc are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Independently and quickly confirmed; the family is well characterised. The pairing mechanism is still not settled, and the Tc is below the cuprates, which tempers lasting-impact claims relative to other candidates.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism is not fully understood.
Practical impact has been limited compared with expectations.
Priority and early follow-up work by other groups are not reflected in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope delivered the first resolved images of the shadow of a supermassive black hole (M87* and Sgr A*), a striking experimental achievement in very-long-baseline interferometry and a direct probe of strong-gravity physics.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed imaging the shadow, Doeleman led the VLBI array building, and Narayan contributed accretion-flow theory. This is a plausible three-person split, but the work is a collaboration of hundreds, and many instrumentation and imaging leaders are not credited. The credit remains disputed.
assessment.maturity: Two black holes imaged and polarisation data published, but the interpretation depends on modelling and the number of independent confirmations is small. Likely premature relative to the other candidates, with future arrays improving the evidence.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and imaging-algorithm attribution are unresolved.
Model-dependence of the extracted parameters.
Independent confirmation by other arrays is not yet available as far as I know.
